record.question: Myeloperoxidase differentiates:
options: acute myeloid from chronic myelocytic leukemia
acute myeloid and acute monocytic from ALL
acute myelomonocytic from acute monocytic leukemia
acute lymphoblastic from acute myeloid leukemia
record.explanation: Answer D: acute lymphoblastic from acute myeloid leukemia. Myeloperoxidase positivity supports myeloid lineage and is generally absent in ALL, so option (d) is the clearest comparison. MPO is not uniformly positive in all AML subtypes, particularly monocytic forms, which makes option (b) overbroad. Source/context note: Avoid implying MPO is positive in every AML subtype; AML with monocytic differentiation can show weak/negative MPO. Reference: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK66019.28/; https://www.cancer.gov/types/leukemia/hp/adult-aml-treatment-pdq. Verified worked solution, unofficial. Original printed wording and option order reviewed; no matching examiner key is asserted.
